MVP

You might say

Let's start with the smallest version that proves the core feature works instead of building everything at once.

The smallest real product or experiment that tests a key product assumption·To test whether freelancers will pay for payment reminders, a team can charge real customers and deliver the reminders manually first. An MVP gathers decision-worthy evidence; it is not a carelessly stripped-down full product.
Know first
PRD
Minimum Viable Product
Test willingness to pay before building the automation

The same hypothesis to testFreelancers will pay for “automatic payment reminders”

Full productBuild everything you can think of first
Invoice NudgeDashboardCustomer managementInvoice systemReminder engineMultiple currenciesTeam permissionsMobile app
  • Features12+ modules
  • InvestmentAbout 6 months
  • ValidationFind out only after launch
MVPTest only the riskiest assumption
Payment reminders for freelancers$29 / monthStart a paid trialReminders are completed manually behind the scenes
  • Features1 core action
  • InvestmentAbout 2 weeks
  • ValidationReal payments in week 1

An MVP is not a thinner full product. It uses the smallest investment to test the assumption most likely to make the product fail.

How an MVP turns effort into useful learning

Choose one risky assumption: Start with the claim that would make the idea fail if it is wrong, such as whether the target user will pay.

Build a minimal credible experience: Keep only the value, participation, and feedback needed to test that claim. A landing page, manual service, or small working version can fit.

Set the evidence and next move: Decide what behavior to observe and what result means continue, change direction, or stop.

What people often confuse

An MVP is not a low-quality product. It must still provide the core value credibly enough to produce evidence, including the safety, privacy, and trust the experiment requires.

You can say this to an AI Agent

“

Our biggest risk is whether freelancers will pay for automatic payment reminders. Design a small paid pilot that tests only that question: specify the price, refund policy, target participants, manual delivery, purchase and renewal evidence, and the result that means continue or stop. Ask for my confirmation before contacting anyone or collecting payment. Free trials, survey claims, or likes can show interest but do not count as payment evidence. Keep privacy and basic trust intact, and do not expand this into a full finance product.
